newsitem.title: USA: Shooting at California McDonald's claims one life.
newsitem.headline: Shooting at California McDonald's claims one life.

text.p: Police searched on Friday for a man who walked into a McDonald's in northern California and while laughing opened fire with a revolver, killing one of the fast-food restaurant's employees and injuring two others.
The unidentified gunman opened fire late on Thursday inside a McDonald's in Vallejo, about 25 miles (40 km) northeast of San Francisco, shooting three young women.

The suspect "strolled" into the restaurant, approached the women at a table and "calmly" began shooting, Lt. Al Lehman said. The gunman, who did not speak during the attack, appeared to be laughing as he pulled the trigger, police said.
All three victims were shot in the head at close range, Lehman said. The gunman, who left the crime scene on foot through the same door he entered, did not try to steal any money from the restaurant.
"He didn't come in to rob the store," Lehman said. "He walked up to three women and shot them and walked out. It just doesn't make any sense. It's extremely bizarre, scary."
Melanie Boncato, 17, the most critically injured in the attack, died at 11:56 a.m. local time Friday, according to the Contra Costa County Coroner's office.
Mercedes Manuel, 21, and Larienel Sapinoso, whose age was unknown but police said was a high school junior, were in stable condition at local hospitals.

The suspect was described by police as a black male, age 29 to 33. He was wearing black pants and a black jacket with yellow and white lettering. A composite sketch of the gunman, who remained at large, was released on Friday.
"At this point we have no motive," Sgt. Herman Robinson said.
